players.product: Data center leasing to hyperscalers and enterprises (Northern Virginia, Richmond, London, Amsterdam, Mumbai; ~325 MW of leasable capacity energizing over the next 24 months) plus hyperscale and neocloud data center decommissioning

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K: as of December 31, 2025 Iron Mountain operated 31 data centers across 21 global markets (directly or through unconsolidated joint ventures) and had leased approximately 97% of the existing 488 MW capacity of its data centers, with an additional 852 MW under construction or held for development and a total potential capacity of 1,340 MW in land and buildings it owns or operates. The company says it is focused on leasing unsold capacity to hyperscale customers and on completing construction and commencing data center leases signed in prior periods.
quarterly_data.figure: 31 data centers in 21 markets; ~97% of 488 MW leased; 852 MW under construction or held for development; 1,340 MW total potential capacity

quarterly_data.signal: 10-K: the Global Data Center Business counts five of the largest global hyperscalers among its customers; data center lease durations vary by customer, with a weighted average lease expiration of 10.3 years as of December 31, 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: five of the largest global hyperscalers as customers; weighted average lease expiration 10.3 years
